neighbours.label: A number+unit (or role noun) used as a pre-modifier inside a compound noun phrase ('a ten minute walk', 'a five-year contract', 'rights defender groups')
fire: The hotel is a ten minute walk from the beach.
She signed a five-year contract with the club.
They booked a two-hour boat tour of the bay.
The farm is about a thirty minute drive north of town.
He is only a two-year-old horse, but he runs fast.
Several women's rights defender networks met in Geneva last week.
We ordered a twelve-inch pizza and two drinks.
It was a six-week course in basic first aid.
quiet: The hotel is a short walk from the beach.
She signed a long contract with the club.
They booked a boat tour of the bay lasting two hours.
The farm lies thirty minutes north of town by car.
He is only a young horse, but he runs fast.
Several women who defend rights met in Geneva last week.
We ordered a large pizza and two drinks.
It was a basic first aid course lasting six weeks.

notes: Probe: 'rights defender groups' 0.74, 'twenty minute drive' 0.59, 'three-year-old technology' 0.49, 'component-style' 0.20; plain noun compounds weaker ('garden chairs' 0.10, 'football club' 0.03); rewrites with the unit after the head ('a drive of twenty minutes', 'three years old') 0.07 and 0.01.
